title: Minimal walkaway scripts and clause maps
body:
Purpose
Quick personal cheat-sheet: tiny scripts and a clause map to use during redlines and live negotiation calls. Not a definitive legal position — use to speed triage and escalate the right items to legal / security.

Top-level priorities (order to push in commercial deals)
1) Data residency & export controls (customer data that triggers export or regulated handling)
2) Model output IP & allowed use (who owns model outputs for customer-provided prompts)
3) Liability cap and carveouts (security/PD/intentional misuse carveouts)
4) Termination & transition assistance (data export, keys, model artifacts)
5) Subprocessor list and onboarding SLA (notice + right to object)

Clause map (quick risk & tactic)
- Indemnity (broad third-party IP claims): Risk = HIGH. Tactic = narrow to direct infringement of customer content / use; push for mutuality or dollar-capped indemnity tied to proven damages. If insist, require control + right to defend.
- Liability cap: Risk = HIGH. Tactic = insist on higher cap for security/breach (e.g., 2-3x fees) or carve out for gross negligence / willful misconduct / data breach and IP indemnity. If customer refuses, push for sub-cap for punitive items rather than unlimited liability.
- Data residency: Risk = HIGH for regulated customers. Tactic = propose region locking + contractual warranty that data will not move outside region without notice. Offer SOC/ISO evidence instead of full contractual guarantees when platform limits apply.
- Model output IP: Risk = MEDIUM-HIGH. Tactic = default: customer owns outputs produced from their prompts. For models trained on third-party data, add assurance clause: we won’t assert ownership over customer outputs; if provider needs rights for improvement, limit to de-identified/aggregated only and allow opt-out.
- Security breach notification + forensics: Risk = HIGH. Tactic = commit to 72-hour initial notice, 30-day root-cause window, and collaborate on customer communication. Avoid promise of specific remediation timelines beyond reasonable efforts.
- Data deletion & export on termination: Risk = MEDIUM. Tactic = require 30–90 days to extract, certified deletion after export. If legacy immutable backups are an issue, add limited retention clause and timeline for purge.
- Subprocessors: Risk = MEDIUM. Tactic = require 30-day notice + right to object for high-risk subprocessors; acceptance via published list acceptable for standard deals.
- Audit rights: Risk = HIGH (if unlimited). Tactic = offer SOC reports and redacted evidence; on-site audits only for enterprise with defined scope and cost sharing.
- SLA credits & uptime: Risk = LOW-MED. Tactic = cap credits to monthly fees; resist unlimited service credits. Add clear definitions for downtime and maintenance windows.

Minimal walkaway scripts (short, repeatable)
- Customer wants unlimited indemnity/liability: "We understand the concern. Our team can accept a targeted indemnity for IP claims tied to our service and a limited liability cap tied to fees. Unlimited exposure would require a separate enterprise underwriting conversation."
- Customer demands on-site audit + broad data access: "We prioritize customer assurance, and we provide SOC2 and supporting reports. For additional audits, we can scope a targeted review under an enterprise audit agreement to protect confidentiality and limit disruption."
- Customer insists on developer-level access to model weights / raw logs: "We can provide agreed-upon export formats and structured logs; full internal artifacts (weights, raw system logs) are sensitive. If you need additional access for compliance, we can discuss a private deployment option with a tailored agreement."
- Customer requires export / residency in a region we don't offer: "We can commit to processing and storing data in available regions; for other regions we offer a phased plan (private deployment or partner region). If timeline is critical, let's flag to Product for feasibility."

Rapid concessions ladder (what to give first -> last)
1) Documentation and SOC/ISO evidence (low cost).
2) Limited additional logging / structured exports (engineering effort/timeboxed).
3) Narrower indemnity or higher liability cap for specific carveouts.
4) Short-term contractual commitments for region/workflow while Product builds full support (requires PM/legal alignment).
5) Source access / on-prem setup = last resort (time/costly, needs sale + SOW).

One-liners to feed engineers / solutions during standups
- "We avoid unlimited liability; ask customer if they will accept a commercially reasonable cap tied to fees."
- "If they need export/residency now, surface to Product — private deployment may be the structured answer."
- "For IP questions: default position is customer owns outputs; highlight new model training claims early."

Hot phrases to use in renegotiation (keeps convo tight)
- "commercially reasonable" (use sparingly, define later)
- "limited to damages arising from direct breaches"
- "mutual indemnity for gross negligence or willful misconduct"
- "we will cooperate in good faith"
- "reasonable efforts to provide export/delivery within X days"

Draft fallback language (very short templates to paste)
- Data residency: "Provider shall process and store Customer Data in the AWS region(s) requested by Customer where such regions are available to Provider; Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to support additional regions upon mutual agreement and subject to separate SOW."
- Output ownership: "Except as set forth in the SOW, Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Prompt Data and Outputs generated solely from Customer Prompt Data."
- Liability carveout: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Provider's liability for claims arising from a Security Breach or Provider's gross negligence shall not be limited to the foregoing cap. For all other claims, Provider's aggregate liability shall not exceed the aggregate fees paid by Customer in the prior 12 months."

Quick reviewer checklist (what I check before sending back to customer)
- Is liability cap present and tied to fees? (Y/N)
- Any unlimited indemnity or uncapped third-party claims? (Y/N)
- Data residency asks that conflict with our regions? (List)
- Any requirement to return/provide source code, weights, or raw logs? (Flag)
- Subprocessor unlimited change/approval? (Flag)
- Audit/on-site rights requested? (Flag)

Open questions for Legal (callout lines to escalate)
- If customer claims ownership of model improvements derived from their prompts, do we need explicit training carveouts?
- Recommended dollar threshold for a security carveout beyond the standard liability cap?
- Template language for shared defense / control of defense in IP indemnities (preferred drafting)?

Notes to self / negotiation heuristics
- Always translate legal ask into engineering impact: "what will it take to deliver this?" (time, logs, region support, cost).
- Push for observable evidence first (SOC, attestations), then contract concessions.
- Use limited live concessions (e.g., 30-day export promise) with explicit SOW path if long-term work needed.

Last-minute scripts (on call)
- "We can sign to this principle, but need a short SOW to scope work and timelines — let's capture acceptance and follow up with a draft."
- "We can add a notice and objection right for subprocessors; can you list your top 3 concerns so we can address them specifically?"

End: keep this doc short and iterative. Update after each negotiation with what actually moved and any templated language that Legal approved.
